nodes.title: Read the scale from a signal input
nodes.why: max is configuration a parent may pass as [max]; input(5) gives it a default of 5 and makes it a signal, so the star list and the aria-labels follow it when it changes.
nodes.alternative: Hard-code five stars, or keep @Input() max = 5 as a plain field.
nodes.tradeoff: The template has to call max(), but values derived from it can be computed signals instead of getters.

nodes.title: Declare the rating as a model
nodes.why: model() creates the rating input and the ratingChange output as one signal the child can read and set, which is the pair [(rating)] binds to.
nodes.alternative: Pair input() or @Input() rating with a ratingChange output and keep the two in step by hand.
nodes.tradeoff: A model emits only when its value changes, so re-selecting the current star sends no event; a parent that needs every click would need an output of its own.

nodes.title: Derive the selectable range from max

anchor.snippet: readonly stars = computed(() => Array.from({ length: this.max() }, (_, i) => i + 1));

nodes.why: The child renders the configured number of one-based choices without hard-coded markup, and the computed rebuilds the array only when max changes.
nodes.alternative: A getter that allocates a new array on every change detection pass, or five literal buttons.
nodes.tradeoff: The values double as @for track keys because they are unique, which holds for any one-through-max range.

nodes.title: Set the model to report the rating
nodes.why: Setting the model updates the stars the child renders and emits ratingChange, so the parent currentRating follows through [(rating)].
nodes.alternative: Assign this.rating = value, which replaces the model with a number and emits nothing, or emit from a separate EventEmitter.
nodes.tradeoff: The child writes a value the parent owns; that is the contract of a two-way binding, and the parent can still change the rating by setting currentRating.

nodes.title: Keep the parent value in a signal
nodes.why: [(rating)]="currentRating" receives the signal itself: Angular reads it for the input and calls set when ratingChange fires, and the hint reads currentRating().
nodes.alternative: A plain currentRating field, which also works with [(rating)] but leaves an OnPush parent stale when the value changes outside its template.
nodes.tradeoff: The template writes currentRating in the binding and currentRating() in the interpolation, a difference that is easy to get wrong.
